title: Beyond Conventional Defenses: Proactive and Adversarial-Resilient Hardware Malware Detection using Deep Reinforcement Learning
problem: Machine learning-enabled hardware malware detection systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that circumvent their detection mechanisms, particularly on tabular processor performance counter data where traditional adversarial learning methods from image classification do not directly apply.
motivation: Adversarial attacks undermine the efficacy of ML-based hardware malware detection methods, creating critical security gaps in hardware protection.
method: A multi-phased framework that first generates adversarial attacks against ML detectors, then uses Deep Reinforcement Learning with Advantage Actor Critic (A2C) to predict adversarial patterns in real-time, fortifies ML models through adversarial training, and employs an RL-based constraint controller using Upper Confidence Bounds (UCB) algorithm to dynamically allocate defense responsibilities among specialized agents based on performance constraints.
key_novelty: Real-time adversarial attack prediction and defense using Deep Reinforcement Learning with dynamic constraint-based allocation of specialized defense agents.
contributions: Multi-phased adversarial learning and defense framework based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
Real-time adversarial attack pattern prediction using Advantage Actor Critic (A2C)
Adversarial training to enhance ML model robustness against combined malware and adversarial attacks
RL-based constraint controller using Upper Confidence Bounds for dynamic defense resource allocation
